# lindfors.no

> Personal site of Emil Lindfors — PhD in technological innovation and senior software engineer in Norway. Writing on Rust, aquaculture technology, sensor systems, and self-hosted infrastructure.

Every post is available as markdown: append `.md` to its slug, or request the post URL with `Accept: text/markdown`. Content may be used as a reference with attribution; it is not licensed for model training.

## Blog posts

- [My citation pipeline died in July and I didn't notice until August](https://lindfors.no/blog/citations-without-zotero.md): A reference manager moved its database, a build script swallowed the error, and every build for a month reported success. Rebuilding the pipeline around DOIs and crossref, and why Zotero stays as the other half.
- [My newsletter promised one-click unsubscribe and answered every one with a 400](https://lindfors.no/blog/newsletter-one-click-unsubscribe.md): Six months of running a self-hosted newsletter: double opt-in with no database, why one-click unsubscribe forced me to stop using my mail server's fan-out, and an RFC 8058 DKIM requirement that ends in an anticlimax.
- [BI is back in its era of ferment](https://lindfors.no/blog/two-defensible-answers.md): Two revenue numbers from one dataset, a month building agent-assisted BI on Wren's semantic layer, and what innovation theory (dominant designs, eras of ferment, lock-in) says to do while the dashboard era is being challenged.
- [Audio on a static site: build-time TTS and the script it reads from](https://lindfors.no/blog/audio-on-a-static-site.md): This post has an audio version, generated at build time with Fish Audio S2.1 Pro and committed next to the PDFs. Picking the model took an afternoon. Deriving something worth listening to from markdown full of code fences took the rest of it.
- [Measuring what a coding agent actually costs](https://lindfors.no/blog/what-my-coding-agent-costs.md): A self-hosted OpenTelemetry stack for LLM usage, built as an OpenObserve experiment for customers who keep telemetry on prem: two months of getting the numbers wrong, 118,469 spans of which 118 were useful, and what Rosenberg's learning by using says about why the price list told me nothing.
- [Forking Codex to talk to any endpoint](https://lindfors.no/blog/forking-codex-for-any-endpoint.md): How we restored the Chat Completions wire API in a Codex fork, so one coding agent drives local Ollama models, OpenRouter, Azure OpenAI with Entra auth, or any EU-hosted provider. The three patches that made it usable, the branch model that keeps the rebases to an hour, and why Baldwin & Clark's design rules say the interface was the thing to fight for.
- [Exploring LLMs so our customers don't have to](https://lindfors.no/blog/which-llm-are-we-allowed-to-use.md): Norwegian businesses started asking their consultants this in 2026, after a year of quietly running Claude Code. Two decisions hidden in one question, why the endpoint matters more than the tool, what it actually costs, and what March's explore/exploit dilemma says about how a company ends up on one vendor without ever deciding to.
- [Proper citations on a static site: Zotero, Rust, and Typst](https://lindfors.no/blog/citations-on-a-static-site.md): How I built a citation pipeline for my Zola blog that reads from Zotero, renders references in HTML, and generates PDFs with Typst. No LaTeX required.
- [Images on a static site: tradeoffs, limits, and a 150-line Rust optimizer](https://lindfors.no/blog/images-on-a-static-site.md): Why I serve images from git instead of object storage, how many I can get away with, and the small Rust tool I built to convert and resize everything to WebP.
- [I replaced Mailchimp with a Rust Worker and a self-hosted mail server](https://lindfors.no/blog/self-hosted-newsletter.md): How I built a complete newsletter system with ~700 lines of Rust, a Cloudflare Worker, and Stalwart mail server. No database, no third-party email service, near-zero cost.
- [I use Typst to generate PDFs of my blog posts and my CV](https://lindfors.no/blog/typst-for-blogging.md): How I replaced LaTeX with Typst to auto-generate downloadable PDFs for every blog post and keep my CV version-controlled. Markdown in, beautiful PDFs out.
- [Why I built my blog with Zola and kept everything in one repo](https://lindfors.no/blog/building-a-personal-blog-with-zola.md): The architecture behind a personal site with self-hosted fonts, dual themes, client-side search, PDF generation, citations, and a newsletter -- all from a single git repo with zero JavaScript frameworks.

## Pages

- [About](https://lindfors.no/about/): Background, research, and contact details.
- [Blog index](https://lindfors.no/blog/): All posts, newest first.
